summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and hepatic encephalopathy was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal and back pain, constipation, and mental fogginess. Imaging revealed severe fecal loading and mild small bowel prominence, consistent with a focal ileus. A urinary tract infection was identified by urinalysis, contributing to her symptoms. She was treated with an aggressive bowel regimen, including enemas and laxatives, which led to significant symptom improvement after a large bowel movement. The UTI was managed with a 7-day course of ciprofloxacin. Oral iron was discontinued due to constipation risk, and she received IV ferrous gluconate for iron deficiency anemia. Her encephalopathy improved with continued lactulose and rifaximin. She was discharged home with new prescriptions for Miralax and PRN bisacodyl, instructions to complete antibiotics, and recommendations to follow up with gynecology for fibroid uterus and monitor hematocrit.
